name: marco-polo
_source: Project Gutenberg #10636 (Vol 1) + #12410 (Vol 2) — Yule & Cordier edition of The Travels of Marco Polo (1903). Chapters are short; entries set mergeChapters:true so the extractor spans multiple chapters per entry.

entries.title: From Constantinople to the East
anchors: It came to pass in the year of Christ 1260, when Baldwin was reigning\s+at Constantinople
Messer Nicolas Polo, the father of my lord\s+Mark, and Messer Maffeo Polo

entries.title: First Audience with the Great Kaan
anchors: When the Two Brothers got to the Great Kaan, he received them with\s+great honour and hospitality
showed much pleasure at their visit

entries.title: The Brothers Set Out with Marco
anchors: When the Two Brothers had received the Legate's letters, they set\s+forth from Acre to return to the Grand Kaan

entries.title: Marco at the Khan's Court
anchors: Now it came to pass that Marco, the son of Messer Nicolo, sped\s+wondrously in learning the customs of the Tartars
as well as their\s+language, their manner of writing

entries.title: Departure from the Great Kaan
anchors: And when the Prince saw that the Two Brothers and Messer Marco were\s+ready to set forth
he called them all three to his presence

entries.title: The Country of Greater Armenia
anchors: HERE THE BOOK BEGINS; AND FIRST IT SPEAKS OF THE LESSER

entries.title: Concerning the City of Cambaluc
anchors: Now there was on that spot in old times a great and noble city called\s+CAMBALUC
which is as much as to say in our tongue "The city of the\s+Emperor

entries.title: The Great City of Kinsay
anchors: When you have left the city of Changan and have travelled for three\s+days through a splendid country
you arrive at the most noble city of KINSAY
